images.title: A digit sliding along the place value chart
images.purpose: Show that when 70, 700 and 7000 are divided by 10 the quotient digit 7 sits one place higher each time the dividend gets a zero.
images.composition: A place value chart with a problem column on the left, three digit columns and three filled rows.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. A table 940 px wide and 530 px high with its top-left corner at x 258 and y 90. It has 4 columns: Problem (400 px wide) and three digit columns of 180 px each, headed Hundreds (amber #E69F00 header cell), Tens (teal #0072B2 header cell) and Ones (reddish purple #CC79A7 header cell), left to right. The header row is 80 px high with the header text in white sans-serif (40 px), and the Problem header is on a light grey #E5E7EB cell with dark text. Below the header are exactly 3 rows, each 150 px high, with thin dark #2B2B2B grid lines. Row 1: Problem cell 70 ÷ 10; the Hundreds and Tens cells are empty; the Ones cell holds the digit 7. Row 2: Problem cell 700 ÷ 10; the Hundreds cell is empty; the Tens cell holds 7 and the Ones cell holds 0. Row 3: Problem cell 7000 ÷ 10; the Hundreds cell holds 7, the Tens cell 0 and the Ones cell 0. The digits are dark #1F2937 sans-serif (64 px), centred in their cells; the problem texts are 44 px, left aligned with 30 px padding. A thin grey #6B7280 arrow (4 px) runs inside the table from the 7 of row 1 to the 7 of row 2 and from the 7 of row 2 to the 7 of row 3, each arrow pointing up and to the left. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a digit in a wrong column, an extra row, or a column heading spelled differently
any equals sign or answer written in the Problem cells
images.takeaway: Each time the dividend gets one more zero, the quotient gets one more zero and its digit 7 moves one place left on the chart.
images.description: A place value chart of the quotients of 70, 700 and 7000 divided by 10, with the digit 7 in the ones, tens and hundreds.
images.context: Concept image for Zeros and Place Value Patterns. The numbers are the plan's own worked example (a 7), not a number of any book question; it follows the idea of the chart in your maths book.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student where the 7 is in each row and how many zeros follow it. The slip to watch: thinking the zeros disappear when dividing by 10.

image_decisions.why: The chart with the digit 7 in three rows shows the pattern of zeros and places that the concept explains.
